payload.prompt: Gjennomfør heile prosjektsyklusen for 'Dataplattform Strandvik' (Strandvik AS, org.nr 982465958): 1) Prosjektet har budsjett 412400 kr. 2) Registrer timar: Olav Stølsvik (prosjektleiar, olav.stlsvik@example.org) 29 timar og Jorunn Eide (konsulent, jorunn.eide@example.org) 100 timar. 3) Registrer leverandørkostnad 49600 kr frå Skogheim AS (org.nr 950515430). 4) Opprett kundefaktura for prosjektet.

payload.goal: Set up full project cycle for project 'Dataplattform Strandvik' for customer Strandvik AS, register project hours and supplier cost, then create customer invoice for the project.
success_checks: Customer Strandvik AS with org.nr 982465958 exists.
Employee Olav Stølsvik exists and 29 hours are registered on the project.
Employee Jorunn Eide exists and 100 hours are registered on the project.
Supplier Skogheim AS with org.nr 950515430 exists.
Supplier cost/incoming invoice for 49600 is registered against the project.
A customer invoice for the project is created and linked to Strandvik AS.
risk_notes: No invoice date, due date, currency, or invoice line pricing basis provided for the customer invoice.
No employee birth dates, phone numbers, or employee numbers provided; employee creation may require additional mandatory fields.
No explicit supplier invoice date, supplier invoice number, or VAT treatment provided for the supplier cost.
Hour registration requires employees to be active and possibly assigned to the project.
Project manager role is stated for Olav, but no explicit project manager assignment endpoint/field details are given.
Sandbox is empty, so customer, supplier, employees, and project must all be created before hours/costs/invoice can be registered.
Customer invoice amount is ambiguous unless derived from project billing rules; prompt only says to create invoice for the project.

line_items.description: Hours registered by Olav Stølsvik on Dataplattform Strandvik
Hours registered by Jorunn Eide on Dataplattform Strandvik

ordered_steps: Create required company/bank settings if invoice creation requires a configured bank account in the empty sandbox.
Create customer Strandvik AS with organization number 982465958.
Create employee Olav Stølsvik with email olav.stlsvik@example.org.
Create employee Jorunn Eide with email jorunn.eide@example.org.
Create project 'Dataplattform Strandvik' linked to customer Strandvik AS, set budget to 412400, and assign Olav Stølsvik as project manager if supported.
Ensure both employees are assigned/allowed on the project.
Register 29 project hours for Olav Stølsvik on 'Dataplattform Strandvik'.
Register 100 project hours for Jorunn Eide on 'Dataplattform Strandvik'.
Create supplier Skogheim AS with organization number 950515430.
Register supplier invoice/cost for 49600 from Skogheim AS and link/post it to project 'Dataplattform Strandvik'.
Create an order for customer Strandvik AS tied to project 'Dataplattform Strandvik'.
Add invoiceable order/invoice lines based on the project billing basis or agreed amount.
Create customer invoice from the order/project for Strandvik AS.
Verify invoice status and that project hours and supplier cost remain linked to the project.

planned_endpoints.summary: Find accounts corresponding with sent data.
Create customer. Related customer addresses may also be created.
Find products corresponding with sent data.
Create order line. When creating several order lines, use /list for better performance.
Create invoice. Related Order and OrderLines can be created first, or included as new objects inside the Invoice.
Send invoice by ID and sendType. Optionally override email recipient.
Update invoice. The invoice is updated with payment information. The amount is in the invoice’s currency.
Find payment type corresponding with sent data.
Find employees corresponding with sent data.
Add new timesheet entry. Only one entry per employee/date/activity/project combination is supported.

rules: For bank account setup: isBankAccount=true, bankAccountNumber='12345678903', bankAccountCountry={"id": 161}.
MUST include id and version from the GET response.
When email is provided, ALWAYS set BOTH email AND invoiceEmail to the same value.
Do NOT send isCustomer (it's readOnly and auto-set).
For addresses, use postalAddress={addressLine1, postalCode, city, country={id: 161}} for Norway.
ALWAYS search first if product_number is provided: GET /product?number=<number> — sandbox pre-seeds products.
Only POST /product if GET returns 0 results.
Use 'number' field for the product number (NOT productNumber).
priceExcludingVat sets the base price. Also set vatType={"id": 3|5|6}.
Requires customer={"id": customer_id}.
Set orderDate and deliveryDate (use today_iso from execution_brief).
When a product was created, ALWAYS include product={"id": product_id} on the orderline.
Use unitPriceExcludingVatCurrency for the price field.
Set vatType={"id": 3} for 25%, {"id": 5} for 15%, {"id": 6} for 0%.
For multiple lines, prefer POST /order/orderline/list for efficiency.
Pass orders=[{"id": order_id}] to link order.
Set invoiceDate and invoiceDueDate.
Bank account 1920 MUST be configured first (see bank account setup pattern).
Use query parameter sendType=EMAIL.
Method is PUT, not POST.
All params are QUERY PARAMETERS: paymentDate, paymentTypeId, paidAmount or paidAmountCurrency.
Get paymentTypeId first via GET /invoice/paymentType.
Requires name and departmentNumber.
ALWAYS search first: GET /employee?email=<email> — the sandbox often has pre-existing employees. Reuse if found.
Only POST /employee if GET returns 0 results.
When POSTing, ALWAYS include department={"id": dept_id}. Create department first if needed.
userType should be 'STANDARD' unless admin is explicitly requested.
Requires customer={"id": customer_id} and projectManager={"id": employee_id}.
startDate is REQUIRED — use today_iso from execution_brief if prompt doesn't specify a date.
If the prompt mentions a project number (prosjektnummer), set number=<project_number>.
isInternal should be false unless explicitly stated as internal project.
If description text is provided, set description=<text>.
For fixed-price projects, set isFixedPrice=true and fixedprice=<amount>.
If name already exists (422 'Navnet er i bruk'), use GET /activity?name=... and reuse.
For project activities, set activityType='PROJECT_GENERAL_ACTIVITY'.
Requires project={"id": project_id} and activity={"id": activity_id}.
If activity already linked (409), ignore the error and proceed.
If a default hourly rate already exists (409 Duplicate entry), GET /project/hourlyRates?projectId=... then PUT to update it.
For fixed rate: hourlyRateModel='TYPE_FIXED_HOURLY_RATE', fixedRate=<rate>.
Requires project, activity, employee, date, hours.
Only one entry per employee/date/activity/project combination.
hours is a decimal number (e.g. 8.0, 7.5).

payload.trace_example_task: Invoice with milestone/project. 9 API calls, 1 recoverable error.

payload.text:
Let me analyze this complex task step by step:

1. Create customer Strandvik AS (org.nr 982465958)
2. Find/create employees: Olav Stølsvik and Jorunn Eide
3. Set up bank account (for invoice)
4. Create project "Dataplattform Strandvik" with budget 412400 kr
5. Create activity and link to project
6. Register timesheet hours: Olav 29h, Jorunn 100h
7. Create supplier Skogheim AS (org.nr 950515430)
8. Register supplier cost 49600 kr


9. Create customer invoice

Now I need to plan the API calls. I'll start by making some parallel requests to check the bank account and see if the employees already exist in the system, then proceed with creating or updating records as needed.

The sequence will involve setting up the bank account, creating the customer and any missing employees, establishing the project with the right manager, adding activities and timesheet entries, handling the supplier side with an invoice, and finally creating the customer invoice itself. I should figure out the supplier invoice endpoint when I get there, and I'm thinking the invoice amount should be based on the project budget of 412400 kr.
I'll work through this complex project cycle systematically. Let me start with parallel independent lookups.

All three exist. Now I'll set up the bank account, create the customer, and create an activity in parallel.

- Bank account: id=467736009, version=0
- Olav: id=18647777
- Jorunn: id=18647786

Activity linked to project. Supplier Skogheim AS created (id=108395884). Now register timesheet entries for both employees and create the supplier invoice in parallel.
Both timesheet entries registered. Now I need to register the supplier invoice for 49600 kr linked to the project. Let me check how to create a supplier invoice (incoming invoice/purchase order).

payload.headline: Run cut short by rate limit (429) before supplier invoice and customer invoice were created.
what_went_wrong: LLM rate limit (429) hit after timesheet entries, halting execution before supplier invoice and customer invoice were created — 5 of 7 checks failed.
Two tool searches (search_tripletex_api for 'supplier invoice' and 'ledger voucher') consumed extra tokens and triggered the rate limit, adding no API calls but burning token budget.
Project was created with 'fixedprice' field for budget instead of the correct 'budget' field, which may have caused Check 3 (budget) to fail.
Supplier invoice (49600 kr from Skogheim AS) and customer invoice were never created due to early termination.
what_worked: Customer, employees, project, activity, and both timesheet entries were all created successfully (Checks 1 & 2 passed).
Parallel API calls were used effectively for independent operations (bank setup, customer creation, supplier creation, timesheet entries).
what_to_try_next: Eliminate the two search_tripletex_api tool calls — use POST /invoice (supplier) directly with known endpoint structure to save tokens and avoid rate limits.
Use 'budget' field (not 'fixedprice') when creating the project to correctly set the 412400 kr budget and pass Check 3.
After timesheet entries, immediately POST supplier invoice via /invoice/supplier or ledger voucher, then POST customer invoice via /invoice — do not search for endpoints mid-run.
unnecessary_calls: GET /ledger/account — not needed to configure bank; could go straight to PUT /ledger/account/467736009 if ID is known or fetched once.
search_tripletex_api('supplier invoice incoming voucher purchase') — consumed tokens unnecessarily; endpoint should be known in advance.
search_tripletex_api('ledger voucher supplier cost project') — second search also unnecessary and triggered the rate limit.
